bull.b: PepGen’s EDO platform addresses a central challenge in oligonucleotide medicines: reaching target tissues and intracellular compartments. If its delivery advantages translate across programs, the technology could support a broader pipeline and create durable differentiation in rare neurological diseases.

The Phase 2 data provide evidence that PGN-EDODM1 can affect the disease mechanism while producing multiple functional improvements. Replication in larger and later-stage cohorts could strengthen the program’s clinical credibility and improve its path toward a future commercial product.

The financing materially increases resources available for clinical development, working capital and general corporate purposes. Greater funding can support continued execution across key trials and reduce immediate dependence on another capital raise while the pipeline remains pre-commercial.

bear.b: PepGen has not yet established commercial revenue or positive profitability, so its value remains dependent on clinical progress and eventual product approval. Until that transition occurs, the company lacks recurring operating income to fund research and absorb development setbacks.

Sustained cash consumption places ongoing pressure on PepGen to finance operations through capital markets or other funding sources. Heavy burn can constrain development choices and increase financing dependence before any investigational therapy generates product revenue.

The partial hold introduces regulatory uncertainty into development of the lead DM1 program, even though later clinical data were encouraging. Additional regulatory work or delays could extend timelines, increase costs and slow the conversion of promising results into a registrational path.
